fields.label: Work Order
fields.description: Required, unlike a line stop. A stop can happen between orders; lost material has to have come from somewhere, and every quantity check here is relative to what this order carried into WIP.

fields.label: Line
fields.description: The order's WIP warehouse, and the source of the transfer. Derived, never typed: there are 0 Workstation records on this floor, so this is the only line dimension the data has, and a copy somebody can edit apart from the order is one that disagrees with it.

fields.label: Quantity
fields.description: In the item's stock UOM. What was lost, not what is left.

fields.label: Reason
fields.description: The same catalogue the stop log uses, filtered to its Loss and Both rows. Today this reason survives only as a free-text paragraph in a Stock Entry's remarks.

fields.label: Stock Entry
fields.description: The DRAFT Material Transfer this record wrote, moving the loss out of WIP and into the scrap warehouse. Accounting submits it in the Desk, exactly as they do today. The link is what makes the two impossible to read apart -- and it is also what makes Frappe refuse to delete the entry while this record still points at it.
